textRestored.prompt: Magnify a differentiable point. Watch the curve straighten — that straightness IS the linearisation.
textRestored.successFeedback: At high magnification the curve is indistinguishable from a straight line. That line is the tangent, and the linearisation is simply USING it instead of the curve. The approximation is good precisely because differentiability promised local straightness in the first place.
textRestored.moreZoomFeedback: Magnify further — the straightening is the point, and it only becomes obvious close in.
textRestored.wrongVerdictFeedback: Both sides settle on the same value, so the limit exists — and the curve is locally straight, which is exactly what makes the tangent a usable stand-in.
